studies.Study: Wang G et al. (2012) [PMID: 22000673] — estimate 1 · Mixed
studies.Reference: Risk factor for clear cell renal cell carcinoma in Chinese population: a case-control study.
studies.Title: Risk factor for clear cell renal cell carcinoma in Chinese population: a case-control study.
studies.Authors: Wang G, Hou J, Ma L, Xie J, Yin J, Xu D, Chang W, Tan X, Su T, Zhang H, Cao G
studies.Population: Chinese subjects recruited in Shanghai; newly diagnosed ccRCC cases and healthy controls
studies.comparison_type: Alcohol consumption (drinkers vs non-drinkers, categories not specified)

sample_size.excerpt: We carried out a hospital-based case-control study to examine the effects of health status, lifestyle, and some genetic polymorphisms on ccRCC risk in Chinese subjects. Between 2007 and 2009, 250 newly diagnosed, histologically confirmed ccRCC cases and 299 sex-, age-matched healthy controls provided complete information including consumption of tea and alcohol, smoking, occupational exposure, body mass index (BMI), hypertension, diabetes, and urolithiasis by face-to-face interview in Shanghai.
sample_size.location: Abstract; total_n derived from reported group counts 250 + 299 = 549

cases.excerpt: Between 2007 and 2009, 250 newly diagnosed, histologically confirmed ccRCC cases and 299 sex-, age-matched healthy controls provided complete information including consumption of tea and alcohol, smoking, occupational exposure, body mass index (BMI), hypertension, diabetes, and urolithiasis by face-to-face interview in Shanghai.

comparison.excerpt: No association was observed between smoking, alcohol consumption, or occupational exposure with ccRCC risk.

studies.Study: Schouten LJ et al. (2016) [PMID: 27340879] — estimate 1 · Mixed
studies.Reference: Alcohol and Dietary Folate Intake and Promoter CpG Island Methylation in Clear-Cell Renal Cell Cancer.
studies.Title: Alcohol and Dietary Folate Intake and Promoter CpG Island Methylation in Clear-Cell Renal Cell Cancer.
studies.Authors: Schouten LJ, Deckers IA, van den Brandt PA, Baldewijns MM, van Engeland M
studies.Population: Netherlands Cohort Study subjects aged 55-69 years

sample_size.excerpt: The Netherlands Cohort Study with a case-cohort design included 120,852 subjects aged 55-69 yr in 1986.

cases.excerpt: Multivariable Cox regression analyses were conducted, stratified according to methylation, including 3980 subcohort members and 297 ccRCC cases.

effect_size.excerpt: Increasing alcohol intake was associated with decreased ccRCC risk, but was not statistically significant; multivariable adjusted hazard ratio (HR) for ≥30 g alcohol/day versus 0 g/day was 0.78 [95% confidence interval (CI): 0.48-1.24], and P-value for trend was 0.46.

confidence_interval.excerpt: Increasing alcohol intake was associated with decreased ccRCC risk, but was not statistically significant; multivariable adjusted hazard ratio (HR) for ≥30 g alcohol/day versus 0 g/day was 0.78 [95% confidence interval (CI): 0.48-1.24], and P-value for trend was 0.46.

design.excerpt: The Netherlands Cohort Study with a case-cohort design

timing.excerpt: After 20.3 yr of follow-up, paraffin-embedded tumor blocks were collected.

exposure_measurement.excerpt: Diet was measured with a food-frequency questionnaire.
